items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1961-10-13
items.q: Jimmy Johnson stayed sick for about six months. And he'd be okay, okay, come up and play with us.

ctx.x: Boy, he passed me a shit day. Fine music. And Jimmy Johnson, Red Bass Music. I mean Caffrey was the only one that didn't read. But the people didn't know it, because we played so well.
What about those other brass bands now? No. No, no, no, those other brass bands at that time. I was wondering about them.

items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1960-04-30
items.q: I didn't know nobody in the band but Kimberl Dial... They sent to St. Louis and got Kimberl Dial and Jimmy Johnson, bass and alto. So Kimberl was the only guy that I knew on the show.

ctx.x: Who was the manager of that Georgia Minstrel? Do you remember anything else about the company? Who else was in the band?

Well, I didn't know nobody in the band but Kimberl Dial. He the one gave me the job because he played with us on the boat after Elliot Taylor taking sick. They sent to St. Louis and got him and the guys, Simon, taking sick too. Simon Moreira taking sick on the boat. And they sent to St. Louis and got Kimberl Dial and Jimmy Johnson, bass and alto. So Kimberl was the only guy that I knew on the show. Yeah. I didn't know none of the musicians. I didn't know. Just got quaming with him afterwards, you know.
